cases.description: Microsoft's documented worked example for the legacy (pre-2010) name: the inverse cumulative beta distribution at probability 0.685470581, alpha=8, beta=10 on [1,3]
cases.expected_note: Microsoft's page publishes this example's result as 2. Independently derived from the documented inverse relationship: A + (B-A)*betaincinv(8,10,0.685470581) = 1 + 2*0.4999999999815714 = 1.9999999999631428 -> 2 at 6 dp; the residue comes from the input probability being a 9-dp rounding of BETADIST(2,8,10,1,3)

cases.description: The median of a Beta(8,10) distribution on the default [0,1] interval
cases.expected_note: Excel documents that omitting A and B uses the standard beta distribution on [0,1]. Independently derived: scipy.special.betaincinv(8,10,0.5) = 0.44234231838132165 -> 0.4423423 at 7 dp
Excel documents: "If probability <= 0 or probability > 1, BETAINV returns the #NUM! error value."
Excel documents: "If alpha <= 0 or beta <= 0, BETAINV returns the #NUM! error value."
Excel documents: "If any argument is nonnumeric, BETAINV returns the #VALUE! error value."
